metadata.title: Master Chronology -- July 3, 1863 (Day 3)
metadata.tick_formula: Tick 451 = 5:00am July 3. Each tick = 5 minutes. Day 3 = ticks 451-675.
sources: Wert, Jeffry D. -- Gettysburg Day 3 (Simon and Schuster, 2001)
Hessler, James A. and Motts, Wayne E. -- Pickett's Charge at Gettysburg (Savas Beatie, 2015)
Pfanz, Harry W. -- Gettysburg: Culp's Hill and Cemetery Hill (UNC Press, 1993)
OR Vol. 27, Parts I and II
Alexander, Edward Porter -- Fighting for the Confederacy (UNC Press, 1989)

events.event: Day 3 opens with Union XII Corps artillery firing on Johnson's Confederates dug into the lower Culp's Hill breastworks. The bombardment opens the longest sustained infantry fight of the battle -- seven hours.
events.flag: Culp's Hill bombardment opens Day 3. XII Corps artillery fires on Confederate positions in Union works.

events.event: Johnson's Confederate division counterattacks to retain the breastworks. Stonewall Brigade, Jones, Nicholls, Steuart assault the XII Corps line. Greene's brigade and returning XII Corps units resist along the hillside works.

Steuart's Confederate brigade makes repeated assaults up the steep hill. 1st Maryland Confederate and 3rd NC suffer heavy casualties. The parallel fight between Union and Confederate Maryland regiments is ongoing here.
events.flag: 1st MD Confederate vs 1st MD Union -- Marylanders vs Marylanders continues through the morning.

events.event: Colgrove's controversial charge. Mudge's 2nd Massachusetts and 27th Indiana ordered to charge across an open meadow toward Confederate positions. Mudge's last words: 'It is murder but it is the order.' Mudge killed leading the charge.
events.flag: Mudge KIA. Colgrove's charge -- show regiments advancing across open ground, repulsed with heavy casualties. Commander succession US-022 activates.

events.event: Both sides fight a grinding attritional battle on Culp's Hill. Johnson's Confederates make twelve distinct assaults. XII Corps holds the upper works throughout. Confederate ammunition running low.
XII Corps counterattacks aggressively. Candy's, Kane's, and Greene's brigades advance to recapture lower works. Johnson's division slowly pushed back. Steuart's brigade suffering severely.
Johnson's Confederate assault on Culp's Hill exhausted. Confederate ammunition nearly expended. Johnson signals Ewell that he cannot continue. Ewell orders Johnson to hold what he has.

Pickett's fresh division moves up behind Seminary Ridge in preparation for the afternoon assault. The three Virginia brigades (Garnett, Kemper, Armistead) form in the woods, invisible to Union observers.
events.flag: Pickett's division forming in the woods -- Bivouac disposition until the charge begins.

events.event: Pettigrew's division (Heth's old command) and Trimble's two brigades (Lane and Scales/Lowrance) positioned on Seminary Ridge left of Pickett. The assault force numbers approximately 12,500 men across a mile front.
Final Culp's Hill fighting. XII Corps retakes most of the contested works. Johnson's remaining Confederates hold a small section of the lower works but are effectively contained.

Culp's Hill fighting finally ends at approximately 11:00am. Johnson's division retires. Twelve Confederate assaults repulsed. Union line on Culp's Hill completely restored. Total Culp's Hill casualties: approximately 3,500 across both days.
events.narrative: The seven-hour Culp's Hill fight was the longest sustained infantry battle of Gettysburg but is overshadowed by Pickett's Charge in popular memory.

events.event: Alexander positions the Confederate artillery along Seminary Ridge for the cannonade. 170 Confederate guns arranged in a two-mile arc from the Peach Orchard north to the Hagerstown Road. Alexander writes two famous messages to Pickett.
events.flag: All Confederate batteries on Seminary Ridge deploy to Online position for the cannonade.

events.event: THE CANNONADE BEGINS. At approximately 1:00pm, two Confederate signal guns fire in sequence. 170 Confederate guns open fire simultaneously -- the largest artillery bombardment in the history of the Western Hemisphere to that date. The sound is heard in Philadelphia, 140 miles away.
events.flag: ALL Confederate batteries on Seminary Ridge firing simultaneously. Ticks 518-542. The most complex artillery animation sequence of the entire battle.
events.narrative: Alexander later wrote that the cannonade was the most magnificent spectacle he ever witnessed. The Union artillery chief Hunt deliberately slowed Union counter-fire to conserve ammunition.

events.event: Hunt deliberately silences Union artillery to conserve ammunition for the infantry assault. Hancock overrules Hunt and orders the guns to keep firing for morale. The disagreement between Hunt and Hancock shapes the eventual repulse.
events.narrative: Hunt's decision to conserve ammunition was tactically correct. Hancock's decision to keep firing boosted infantry morale but depleted artillery reserves.

events.event: Confederate artillery fire overshooting Cemetery Ridge -- most shells landing behind the Union line near Taneytown Road. Union artillery casualties lighter than expected. Meade's headquarters nearly hit.
events.narrative: The Confederate tendency to overshoot was a significant tactical failure -- the cannonade inflicted far less damage on the Union infantry than Lee and Alexander had hoped.

events.event: Alexander's first message to Pickett: 'For God's sake come quick or we cannot support you -- ammunition nearly exhausted.' Pickett shows it to Longstreet. Longstreet cannot speak -- nods his head. The charge is set in motion.
events.narrative: Longstreet later wrote: 'I could not speak. I bowed in answer.' His reluctance to order the charge is evident in every account.

events.event: Alexander's second message to Pickett: 'I would not make the charge now -- but the order has been given and the troops are already moving.' Pickett's division steps out of the woods.

Union artillery falls silent -- Confederate infantry interpret this as success of the cannonade. In fact Hunt has ordered silence to conserve ammunition. Confederate infantry begin dressing their lines in the open.
Stannard's Vermont Brigade (I Corps) takes position south of The Angle on Cemetery Ridge. Stannard has a clear view of Kemper's right flank. He is already planning the flanking maneuver.

PICKETT'S CHARGE BEGINS. The entire Confederate assault force -- approximately 12,500 men in a mile-wide front -- steps off Seminary Ridge in Line of Battle heading east across the open fields toward Cemetery Ridge. The most famous infantry assault in American history.
events.flag: ALL assault brigades in Line of Battle advancing east from Seminary Ridge. Ticks 538-553. The central animation sequence of the entire project.

events.event: Union artillery opens with solid shot then shell as the Confederate line advances across the open ground. Each discharge tears gaps in the Confederate line. The attackers close ranks and keep moving.

BROCKENBROUGH COLLAPSES. The far Confederate left (Brockenbrough's Virginia brigade) breaks and retreats under flanking fire from the 8th Ohio's advanced skirmish position. Pettigrew's left flank is now exposed.
events.flag: Brockenbrough breaks while other brigades still advance. Show C-III-2-2 in Chaotic Retreat while adjacent brigades maintain Line of Battle. Diverging movement required.

events.event: Confederate assault line reaches the Emmitsburg Road and crosses the fencing. Heavy casualties from Union artillery and musketry. Kemper's brigade begins obliquing left toward the Copse of Trees -- exposing its right flank.

STANNARD'S FLANKING ATTACK. Stannard's Vermont brigade wheels left 90 degrees and pours enfilade fire into Kemper's exposed right flank. The 13th and 14th Vermont fire into the Confederate right. Kemper's brigade takes devastating flank fire.
events.flag: Stannard's flank -- 13th and 14th VT wheel left. 16th VT will make SECOND wheel against Wilcox. Two distinct bearing changes for 16th VT.

events.event: Kemper severely wounded in the Confederate assault. Mayo assumes brigade command. Kemper briefly captured, then rescued by his men. Commander succession CS-006 activates.

Pettigrew's Confederate brigades (26th NC, 11th NC, 47th NC, 52nd NC) reach the stone wall on Cemetery Ridge north of The Angle. Union II Corps (Smyth, Hays) fires at close range. 12th NJ fires buck-and-ball at point-blank range.

Garnett's Confederate brigade reaches the stone wall at The Angle. Heavy casualties from canister. Garnett rides on horseback (too ill to walk) -- conspicuous and exposed. The two lines exchange fire at close range across the wall.
events.flag: Garnett's brigade at The Angle wall. Garnett on horseback is visible. Webb's Philadelphia Brigade firing across the wall.

events.event: GARNETT KIA. Shot from his horse at The Angle -- his body never officially identified after the battle. Marshall killed leading Pettigrew's brigade. Multiple Confederate commanders fall almost simultaneously.
events.flag: Garnett KIA tick 550. Marshall KIA tick 550. Commander successions CS-005 and CS-010 activate.

events.event: ARMISTEAD LEADS MEN OVER THE WALL. Armistead places his hat on his sword as a guide and leads his brigade over the stone wall at The Angle -- the deepest Confederate penetration of the battle. Approximately 150-200 men cross with him.
events.flag: HIGHEST PRIORITY ANIMATION. Armistead crosses the wall with hat on sword. Show C-I-3-3 crossing the wall into the Union position. The High Water Mark of the Confederacy.

events.event: ARMISTEAD MORTALLY WOUNDED. Shot moments after crossing the wall -- while touching a Union gun with his hand. Falls beyond the stone wall among Union troops. Armistead asks for Hancock to be brought to him. Hancock also wounded at this moment.
events.flag: Armistead falls BEYOND the wall. Must be shown inside Union position. Hancock wounded simultaneously. Commander succession CS-007 activates.

events.event: CUSHING KIA. Lieutenant Cushing, serving his last two guns at The Angle, shot through the mouth and killed. Sergeant Fuger assumes command of the shattered battery. Commander succession US-023 activates.
events.flag: Cushing KIA tick 553. Last two guns at the wall. Commander succession US-023 activates.

events.event: Cowan's Union battery fires canister into Armistead's men at approximately 50 yards -- devastating close-range fire. Union infantry closes from multiple directions. The Confederate penetration is contained and then driven back.
events.flag: Cowan's canister -- battery placed approximately 50 yards from Confederate breakthrough.

events.event: The Confederate penetration is broken. Armistead's men streaming back over the wall or surrendering. Devereux's 19th Massachusetts and others pour into the breach. The Angle is secured.
events.flag: Confederate repulse at The Angle. C-I-3-3 shows Chaotic Retreat. Union line restored.

events.event: Along the entire line the Confederate assault collapses. Pettigrew's brigades fall back. Trimble (wounded) orders retreat. The survivors stream back toward Seminary Ridge. Lee rides forward to meet them: 'It is all my fault.'
events.narrative: Lee's acknowledgment -- 'It is all my fault' -- is one of the most famous statements of the war. He met his broken men personally and attempted to rally them for a Union counterattack that never came.

events.event: 16TH VERMONT SECOND WHEEL. Stannard's 16th VT wheels again -- now against Wilcox's and Lang's Confederate brigades advancing in belated support of Pickett. The double enfilade effectively seals the repulse on the south end.
events.flag: 16th VT SECOND bearing change. First wheeled against Pickett's right. Now wheels against Wilcox. Two direction changes across ticks 546 and 558.

events.event: EAST CAVALRY FIELD. Stuart's cavalry (Hampton, Fitz Lee, Chambliss) attacks east of Gettysburg attempting to reach the Union rear during the main assault. Gregg and Custer's Michigan Brigade block the advance.
events.location: East Cavalry Field (3 miles east of Gettysburg)
events.flag: East Cavalry Field action begins. Stuart's cavalry in Line of March then Mounted Cavalry. Custer and McIntosh deploy to block.

events.event: CUSTER'S CHARGE. Custer personally leads the Michigan Brigade in a mounted charge shouting 'Come on you Wolverines!' The charge stops Stuart's advance. Hampton wounded in melee -- sabre cut to head. Commander succession CS-017 activates.
events.flag: Custer's mounted charge. Michigan Brigade from Line of March to Charging Line. Hampton wounded. CS-017 activates.

events.event: Stuart's cavalry repulsed at East Cavalry Field. The Confederate cavalry's last chance to reach the Union rear during Pickett's Charge is gone. Pennington's Union horse artillery fires in support throughout.

KILPATRICK'S CHARGE. Kilpatrick orders Farnsworth's cavalry brigade to charge Confederate infantry south of the battlefield. Farnsworth protests: the charge is suicidal over rocky terrain against formed infantry.
FARNSWORTH KIA. Farnsworth leads the doomed charge and is killed -- a general for only four days. The charge accomplishes nothing. Kilpatrick's decision is universally condemned.
events.flag: Farnsworth's charge and death. U-CAV-3-1 in Charging Line then Chaotic Retreat.

events.event: Meade considers a counterattack. Hancock (wounded) urges one. Meade decides the army is too disorganized and depleted. The counterattack that might have destroyed Lee's army does not happen.
events.narrative: Meade's failure to counterattack after Pickett's repulse is his most criticized decision of the battle.

events.event: Lee begins organizing his army for defense -- expecting Meade's counterattack. When it doesn't come, Lee begins considering withdrawal. Ewell, Hill, and Longstreet ordered to consolidate.
Both armies largely stationary. Union troops bury the dead and collect wounded. Confederate artillery conserves remaining ammunition. Lee confers with his corps commanders about the retreat.
Lee orders the retreat to begin on July 4. Imboden's cavalry will escort the enormous wagon train of wounded -- 17 miles long. Lee takes full responsibility for the defeat.
events.narrative: Imboden described Lee at this moment: 'I never saw a man so agitated in my life' -- pacing back and forth, saying over and over 'Too bad. Too bad. Oh, too bad.'

events.event: Rain begins. Both armies exhausted. The Battle of Gettysburg is effectively over. Union casualties: approximately 23,000. Confederate casualties: approximately 28,000. Total: ~51,000 in three days.

END OF THE BATTLE. Total Confederate losses approximately 37% of the army engaged. Total Union losses approximately 25%. The Confederate Army of Northern Virginia will never again mount a strategic offensive into the North. The High Water Mark of the Confederacy has passed.
events.narrative: Gettysburg, combined with Vicksburg's fall on July 4, marks the turning point of the Civil War. The Confederacy would fight on for nearly two more years but the strategic initiative passed permanently to the Union.
